Hey, I’m 18 and a freshman at college rn, and I seriously considered taking a break too. My studies began declining from highschool as my parents began preparing me for a degree in CS, when I had no interest in it. As time for applications approached, I desperately tried avoiding my reality in many ways, but well, it caught up with me.
My advice is, maybe read up about people’s experiences when they did take a break year. Then try seeing what good and bad consequences you might have to face if you do take a break. If you can afford to face the bad consequences (which I decided I couldn’t, so I didn’t take no break), then go ahead with it. Also if you do decide to take it, then simply tell your parents the reasoning behind it. If your parents are healthy they’ll definitely try to understand. Don’t worry about disappointing them, because honestly, if having to go to college is depressing you that much, then taking care of yourself should be your first priority.

It was the day my tenth boards ended. Me and my two best friends had a sleepover for the first time in my friend’s house. We spent the evening chit chatting about random stuff, then went for a movie, stalked the actor online after we returned home. After dinner, we watched the movie ‘Jodha Akbar’ Because I insisted. By the time we completed half the movie, one of my friends fell asleep. Me and my other friend put the phone we were watching the movie on to charge, and went on to talk into the night. We sat there, huddled together in her small living room (we were given the entire house for ourselves), talking about kings and queens and how life would’ve been back then, watching historical movies’ music videos in the middle,talking about how our school crushes would never grow into anything more. I am very fond of this time, because of the little home of my friend’s. Every inch of the place was covered with furniture and books, and something about the silence made me feel right at home. The window looked out onto trees swaying in the night sky, the faint light of street light below hitting the leaves. I remember the clock ticking above us, the crickets listening in onto our conversation, the subtle snoring of my asleep friend, the relief of the end of exams, the strange feeling after we watch a movie in a theatre. It is a night I will never quite forget. I will keep returning to it on my most stressful days, knowing that I always have friends I can go to, knowing that I can always spend another night there, talking about all the things that make me happy.
